subject: Dedicated capacity demo — slot coordination & latency checklist
messages:
From: Marco Alvarez <marco@corelytics.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: demo for dedicated capacity (self-signup)

Hi Kimberly,

We just spun up a trial on your site (signup id: SS-9082) and got routed to Ben — thanks for the quick follow-up. Our infra team is evaluating Dedicated capacity because we need predictable throughput for a summarization endpoint used in our customer-facing product.

Quick context:
- Target sustained throughput: ~6k requests/minute (roughly 100 rps) across peak windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for 128-token responses is ideal; p99 targets are less strict but we'd like to understand tail behavior.
- Model: planning to evaluate a 13B open model with 8-bit quantization.

Can we schedule a dedicated-capacity walkthrough to see throughput sizing, warm pool behavior, and failure fallbacks? We're PST-based; afternoons work best for us (after 1pm). I'll attach a sample payload file so you can size the demo if useful.

Thanks,
Marco
Principal Engineer, Corelytics
[Attachment: corelytics_workload_v1.json (application/json, 28KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: demo for dedicated capacity (self-signup)

Hi Marco — great to meet you and welcome to Redwood. Thanks for including the throughput/latency targets and the payload — that helps a lot.

We can run a focused 45-minute dedicated-capacity walkthrough that covers: sizing math for steady-state QPS, autoscale/warm-pool behavior, p95/p99 latency profiles (demo with your sample), and fallback policies when capacity hits limits.

Availability windows (PST):
- Tue 2025-05-12, 2:00–3:00pm
- Tue 2025-05-12, 4:00–4:45pm (tight)
- Wed 2025-05-13, 11:00am–12:00pm

Before the call, could you confirm:
1) an estimate of average tokens per request (we'll use this to size the GPU working set),
2) whether you need GPU isolation (dedicated pool) or tenant-shared reserved capacity, and
3) if you want us to include a short segment on cost-optimization (batching + KV cache).

Looping in Priyom from our demos team to own the calendar/tech prep. I've attached a short pre-call checklist we typically use.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise SDR Lead — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_precall_checklist.pdf]
